extracted.intended_audience: people who need to write or generate jokes (speakers, social-media writers, standup comics, comedy writers experimenting with AI)
extracted.subtask_description: Using an LLM (or an LLM-based app) to generate jokes, either as a rapid idea generator or as a co-writer, by applying explicit professional joke-writing techniques to the model. Focuses on getting original, surprising jokes rather than generic outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surprise / originality
rubrics_metrics.description: A joke has to be surprising to be funny; ChatGPT and other AI language models can’t write good jokes because they can only mimic the surface patterns of jokes that they’ve been trained on, and therefore can’t write jokes that are actually surprising.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate jokes for genuine surprise and novelty rather than surface-level joke patterns. Treat outputs from generic LLMs skeptically because they tend to reproduce rehearsed patterns rather than produce fresh, surprising punchlines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Explicit structure / teach the model how to build a joke
rubrics_metrics.description: An AI system can write a joke if it’s explicitly told how to structure a joke.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provide the model with concrete, professional joke-writing structures (beats, setups, punchlines, misdirection). Instruct the model step-by-step rather than asking for an end-to-end joke with no structural guidance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hybrid human+AI workflow (AI as co-writer)
rubrics_metrics.description: Use AI as a hybrid tool: Witscript is a hybrid of an LLM and professional joke-writing techniques (i.e., sending an LLM to 'joke school').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prefer a co-writing approach where human expertise (techniques, judgment, editing) is combined with the model’s generative speed. Use the app to kickstart creativity or produce drafts, then have a human refine for timing, voice, and funniness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use-case / audience tailoring
rubrics_metrics.description: You may need jokes for different contexts — a speech, social media, or standup comedy — and the joke should fit that context.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Tailor joke length, tone, and subject matter to the intended medium and audience (e.g., short, attention-grabbing lines for social media; longer set pieces for standup; targeted lines for speeches). Specify context when prompting the model.

rubrics_metrics.name: Quality improvement via specialized instruction/training
rubrics_metrics.description: Training or instructing an LLM with professional joke-writing techniques (the author's book/classes) produces better results — Witscript was created by teaching those techniques to an AI system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Invest in domain-specific prompt engineering or a specialized model/app that embeds professional comedy methods rather than relying on off-the-shelf, general-purpose LLM outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speed and productivity (efficiency)
rubrics_metrics.description: AI can be used to 'write original jokes fast' and to 'kickstart your comedy creativity.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use AI tools to rapidly generate ideas and variants, then apply human editorial judgment to select and refine the best material. Measure success by how quickly useful, editable joke material is produced rather than by raw humor of first drafts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid treating AI as a full replacement
rubrics_metrics.description: You could pay somebody to write jokes, study joke writing, or use AI — but AI alone won’t produce good jokes; professional techniques and human input are required.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not rely solely on generic LLM outputs as finished jokes. Use AI outputs as inputs to a human-led creative process; prioritize human editing and technique application to turn AI drafts into genuinely funny material.
